# Pi adapter for the reviewed pstack source

The behavior source is the immutable `vendor/upstream/0.15.17/pstack/` Markdown snapshot at `978ca6e9c0e012047cd5058b8e829240336e704e`. The generated eleven core entrypoints retain its instructions, with platform adaptations in a separate prelude. Do not summarize away upstream rules. Local changes outside these eleven workflows are not semantically audited by this work.

Apply user instructions and repository authority first. Apply the pinned upstream decision rules next, subject only to the explicit overrides below. Never run a Cursor command literally or assume a missing capability completed. Read referenced source Markdown through `pstack_skill` with `upstream/skills/<skill>/...` resource IDs; consume every page. Original relative links resolve within that snapshot. Other plugin skills, private APIs, scripts, control drivers, cloud resources and manifests are not supplied by the Markdown snapshot. ## Platform substitutions

- Pi Skill frontmatter uses the resource directory name in lowercase kebab case (upstream `Poteto Mode` becomes `poteto-mode`). The upstream body and the original snapshot frontmatter remain intact.

- Task and cloud workers map to `pstack_agents` and `pstack_workflow` Pi AgentSessions. The parent keeps playbook ownership. Parallel writers require separate Git worktrees; integrated delivery requires an explicit integrator followed by verification of the combined artifact. These are local processes, not cloud VMs.
- Resolve model roles through `~/.pi/agent/pstack-native/models.json` (or PSTACK_NATIVE_HOME) and available Pi provider/model selectors. For panels name every seat explicitly. Use `pstack_semantics` panel preflight; no silent provider/model fallback. Unavailable models block the affected seat and must be reported. This deliberately replaces upstream family-default fallback.
- `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc`, `.cursor/skills` and Cursor's plugin paths map to Pi configuration and the bundled snapshot. They are not files the Pi worker should create in a user's repository.
- Custom Mode maps to sticky `/poteto-mode`. `/loop` maps to `/pstack-loop`, which needs an active Pi host. Cloud-root hourly execution and exact delivery across a crash are unavailable; report this limitation before promising unattended audit coverage.
- Use a named available CLI/UI driver for real-surface proof. If no driver can reach the surface, return BLOCKED or inconclusive with the exact reason. Unit tests, fake providers, a worker's report or CI alone cannot replace the live lane.

## Explicit policy deviations

- Any head OR base change invalidates native verification and every round receipt, even when stable patch IDs match. Re-run lanes on the current exact pair. Upstream's build-noise/patch-ID reuse exception is intentionally disabled; the stricter native ledger policy remains in force.
- Read-only reviewer/verifier sessions inspect confined source and evidence; they cannot run shell commands. Deterministic commands run in the native verification runner or an authorized writable lane. A separate actor inspects the receipts; a writer cannot countersign its own work.
- The native arena template evaluates each candidate with separate judge nodes rather than one cross-judge that sees all candidates. Use an explicit DAG for the upstream single-cross-judge choreography. Native specialized templates are mechanisms, not automatic completion of a named upstream playbook.
- Native swarm templates cover partition and best-of race. Mixed/first-pass/rank-all require an explicit DAG and declared selection policy; do not silently relabel best-of as first-pass.
- The native autopilot templates prepare local DAG artifacts. Full owner lifecycle, early ready PR, decisions.tsv/children.tsv, periodic audit, rebase discipline, root countersigns and stop propagation remain obligations of the coordinator. The stack template is not a delivered remote PR stack; use stack-plan/stack-open with correct parent worktrees.
- Babysit stops before merge, even when checks are green. Opening a PR does not start a babysit. An explicitly assigned full-autonomy owner may begin its assigned loop after its code-ready report; other agents finish their phase or stack before the handoff. Autopilot-stack stops before shipping. Full-autopilot still needs the operator's go; operator-reserved items never merge automatically. Use `pstack_semantics` round checks before a clean verdict, then native Frontier, ledger and authorization checks for any shipping operation. The round check neither attests the truth of supplied receipts nor authorizes a remote action.

## Unsupported operations

`Cursor-private-PR-provenance`, `Cursor-watch-READY`, `Cursor-cleanup-plugin` and `Bugbot-pass-dismissal` are unsupported. Querying one through `pstack_semantics` fails with an explicit error. GitHub/Origin state and native watch states are usable alternatives only within their own evidence boundary, not proof that a Cursor operation ran. Private provenance, queue verdicts and pass-based dismissal cannot be inferred from green CI. Do not mark a workflow complete when one of its required operations is unavailable.

## Evidence boundary

`SEMANTICS.json` records critical-rule mappings, exact source ranges, deviations, test references and review fingerprints. Inventory counts, mapping coverage, deterministic receipt tests, fake-provider Pi lifecycle tests and real-model runs are separate evidence levels. No mapping asserts complete chat/model equivalence. Updating a fingerprint records review work; it is not semantic approval. The reviewed baseline stays at 0.15.17 until explicit maintainer semantic sign-off. Candidate 0.15.32 remains separate.

## Pinned upstream instructions

Source: cursor/plugins@978ca6e9c0e012047cd5058b8e829240336e704e, pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/shipping.md. The following body is retained verbatim.

## Steps

### Shipping

**You own what lands. Verify each PR independently, land only the verified run from the root, then keep your hands off the queue.**

This is the half after `playbooks/babysit.md`.

1. **Resolve the forge, then verify every PR independently.** GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, use `origin pr ...` for PR view, watch, edit, and merge operations. Otherwise stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Never require Graphite (`gt`). One subagent per PR, not batched, each a Cursor cloud agent, each exercising the real surface with the matching control skill (such as `control-ui` or `control-cli` from `cursor-team-kit`) against parent versus head. Each returns `PASS`, `PASS+NOTES` or `FAIL` and posts that verdict on its own PR. Safe means a verdict from an agent that did not write the code. CI green is not a verdict, and an approving bot review is not a verdict.
2. **Land only the contiguous verified run rooted at the bottom.** Walk up from the lowest unmerged PR and stop at the first one without a passing verdict, where both `PASS` and `PASS+NOTES` pass. A verified PR sitting above an unverified one is not landable. Report the ceiling as a PR number and say what breaks the chain.
3. **Re-check that each verdict still describes the patch.** Record the verdict head SHA, base SHA, and stable `git patch-id` of that PR's base-to-head diff. A rebase or base retarget rewrites SHAs and can silently invalidate a verdict without touching a check. Before landing a PR, compare the recorded patch-id with its current base-to-head patch-id. When the two patches differ only in tests, docs, or lint config, build what each lane ran. Build it twice at the verdict SHA and once at the current head. A difference is noise if the two builds at the verdict SHA also show it, or if it is an embedded commit SHA. Judge each difference, not each file, and report each kind of noise with its files. If only noise differs, that lane's result stays valid, and checks and a review of the change run fresh. Do not reuse a lane result from a dev server or from anything else with no build output. Rerun that lane. Re-verify anything else when the patch changed. When it did not, keep the code verdict but re-run mergeability and CI at the current head. Never use matching commit messages or a green check from an older SHA as a substitute.
4. **Prepare only the bottom PR.** Fetch current trunk. Rebase the lowest verified branch onto the exact trunk tip when needed, push it, and retarget only that PR to trunk with `origin pr edit <pr> --base <trunk>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <trunk>`. Re-run step 3 after the push. Do not retarget, arm, or merge descendants yet.
5. **Land one PR at a time.** If the bottom PR is mergeable now, squash it with `origin pr merge <pr> --squash` or `gh pr merge <pr> --squash`. If requirements are still running and the user asked for merge-when-ready, arm only that PR with `origin pr merge <pr> --squash --auto` or `gh pr merge <pr> --squash --auto`. Origin's `--auto` is Origin merge-when-ready. GitHub's `--auto` is GitHub auto-merge. Wait for that PR to merge before preparing the next one.
6. **Do not read GitHub `autoMergeRequest` as stack readiness.** At most it says GitHub auto-merge was requested for one GitHub PR. It does not prove Origin merge-when-ready is armed, that a descendant is queued, that a patch verdict is current, or that the contiguous stack is safe. Confirm the active forge's state for the current bottom PR, and say that the state is unknown if the active forge cannot report it.
7. **Recompute after every merge.** Fetch trunk, confirm the merged SHA is present, drop the merged PR from the frozen bottom-to-top list, and inspect the new bottom PR's base, head, checks, and patch-id. A host may retarget a child automatically, but do not assume it did. Repeat steps 3 through 6 for that one PR. Independent work stays outside this chain and ships on its own.
8. **Watch the current frontier until it merges or fails. Do not mutate the queue around it.** With Origin, use `origin pr view <pr> --checks --comments` and `origin pr checks <pr> --watch`, then re-read the PR until it reports merged or blocked. With GitHub, use `scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr --queued-stack --stack-prs <bottom>` only as an event wake and poll `gh pr view <pr> --json state,mergedAt,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup,autoMergeRequest` after each wake, ignoring `READY` until `mergedAt` is non-null or `state` is `MERGED`. Only then run step 7. Hard-fail only when `state` is `CLOSED` with no `mergedAt`, a required check concludes `FAILURE` or `CANCELLED` and blocks merge after auto-merge is no longer pending, or `mergeStateStatus` is `UNSTABLE` or `DIRTY` with no auto-merge pending. `BLOCKED` while checks are pending or auto-merge is armed is not failure. Do not use Babysit's queued `WAITING`/`merge-queue` stop condition here. Hold the watch under `/loop` in dynamic mode. Report each merge and the new ceiling. If the queue stalls, diagnose before mutating.
9. **Stop at the ceiling.** When the verified run is merged, report what landed, what the next unverified PR is, and what verifying it would take. Extending the run is a new pass through step 1.

**Reply:** the verified run and its ceiling, each PR's verdict and who produced it, what you armed and how you confirmed it, what landed, and what the next gap needs.


## Pi execution tools

Use `pstack_agents` for one child and `pstack_workflow` / `pstack_graph` for an explicit DAG. Roles are `architect`, `worker`, `reviewer`, `verifier`, `synthesizer` and `integrator`. Parallel writers use isolated worktrees, then an integrator. A verifier directly depends on the artifact owner. Inspect workflow status on recovery; completed nodes are not replayed. Check remote state before retrying external effects. `pstack_worktrees` cleans only owned clean worktrees.
